newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL AND ENGLISH F.A. PLEDGE SUPPORT FOR ADAMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL AND ENGLISH F.A. PLEDGE SUPPORT FOR ADAMS.

text.p: Arsenal pledged their support for club skipper Tony Adams on Sunday following the player's public admission he was an alcoholic.

Adams, who will be 30 next month, told the club of his problems on Friday and was allowed to take time off from training on Sunday to spend time with his family. He has not played this season because of a knee injury.
The tall central defender, who has had a drink problem for several years, has disclosed he started drinking again over disappointment at England's Euro 96 semifinal defeat by Germany.
"I have been attending Alcoholics Anonymous," he said on Saturday. "It's OK. I had to face up to the problem when I looked at myself in the mirror and didn't like what I saw."

The former England captain, who served a jail term for drink-driving offences five years ago and who has been involved in a number of drink-related incidents, had been dry for the four months leading up to the penalty shoot-out defeat at Wembley in June.

But with his misery compounded by domestic problems -- he split up with his wife Jane after she began receiving treatment for cocaine addiction -- the "quiet drink" turned into a return to the heavy drinking problems he had recognised in February.
He told of the extent of his problem to team mates on Friday and after training with the Arsenal players over the weekend he faced the media to explain he was "on the road to recovery".
While the other Arsenal players were training in preparation for Monday's premier league game with Sheffield Wednesday, Adams was an absentee from the club's training ground.
Pat Rice, in charge of the club after caretaker boss Stewart Houston quit on Friday, insisted there was nothing to be read into Adams's absence.
"Tony has worked hard in the past two days and we've let him spend today with his family," said Rice. "We hope to arrange a friendly match for him to play in during the early part of next week.
"What Tony has given to this club is unbelievable and there were never any reservations in giving something back to him when he needs it.
"The best result we could ever hope for is to see him out on the pitch playing for the first team again. Hopefully that will not be too long."
The English F.A. also offered sympathy at the news of Adams's relapse and their spokesman David Davies said: "Tony Adams can be assured of our total support in sorting out any problems he has.
"His role as England captain during Euro 96 has been widely and rightly recognised as considerable."
Gordon Taylor, chief executive of the players' union the Professional Footballers' Association, also pledged his backing for Adams.

"I will be making contact with Tony this week and offering the support of the PFA and any help we can provide," said Taylor. "I have the greatest admiration for him as a person, a captain and a player.
"Our position with Tony is the same as it was for Paul Merson when he confessed his problems with drink, drugs and gambling, and just as it would be with any of our members.
"This is a very personal situation, and the decision to want help has to come from the player himself."
